A second US national has been evacuated to Germany for treatment, and the Trump administration is barring Americans in the DRC from returning to the US on commercial flights. Separately, UK health officials are warning of a rapid rise in imported Zika virus cases, and Los Angeles County has reported its first West Nile virus case of 2026.

clusters.state_of_play: The death toll from the major wildfire in southern Spain's Andalusia/Almería region stands at 13, with nationality now confirmed: five Britons, three Belgians, one French national, and one Spanish national among the dead; DNA identification was required for badly burned victims. Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez visited the wildfire site in Almería, met firefighters and emergency crews, and called for Spain to strengthen prevention measures. Victims' families have alleged they received no evacuation order from authorities. The missing count has been revised down to 10 as the fire stabilised, allowing hundreds of evacuees to return to their homes; the blaze has burned around 7,000 hectares (~25 sq miles). British survivor Malcolm Timbrell, 70, from the village of Bédar, told of surviving in his car while his wife Annette Kilgore and friends died trying to run to safety. A British man died while on the phone to his wife after returning to rescue cats, and two British hikers were found alive but badly burned in a ravine. A 93-year-old British woman admitted Friday with 20% burns to Torrecardenas University Hospital died Sunday night. Separately, a wildfire of 'exceptional scale' is burning near Paris amid France's third heat wave since May, adding to Europe's worsening fire crisis. In the UK, major incidents have been declared in North Wales and in Glossop, Derbyshire in the Peak District, with at least 10 wildfires burning across Wales and 19 separate wildfires being tackled across the UK overall. A wildfire near Conwy Mountain prompted evacuation of 36 homes. A 20-year-old woman, Shania Care-Slede, has been charged with aggravated arson in connection with a UK moor fire for which a major incident was declared. The Met Office's Fire Severity Index identifies parts of southern England — including around Chichester and Bognor Regis in West Sussex — as most at risk. An 'exceptional' wildfire warning has been issued for parts of the UK as a heatwave, now entering its second week in some areas, is forecast to last at least another week; hosepipe bans are in effect. The National Fire Chiefs Council warned that hot dry weather 'significantly increases wildfire risk.' Climatologist Jean-Pascal Van Ypersele warned 'We are not prepared enough for the conditions that fuel these fires.' In a separate legal development, Sánchez's brother David has been banned from holding public office for nine years after being convicted of administrative misconduct relating to his hiring by a socialist-led council in Extremadura.

items.title: Wildfire of "exceptional scale" burning near Paris

ledger.what_new: A wildfire of 'exceptional scale' is burning near Paris amid a third heat wave since May.
ledger.unique: New major wildfire near Paris; third heat wave since May.

clusters.state_of_play: The death toll from the major wildfire in southern Spain's Andalusia/Almería region stands at 13, with nationality now confirmed: five Britons, three Belgians, one French national, and one Spanish national among the dead; DNA identification was required for badly burned victims. Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez visited the wildfire site in Almería, met firefighters and emergency crews, and called for Spain to strengthen prevention measures. Victims' families have alleged they received no evacuation order from authorities. The missing count has been revised down to 10 as the fire stabilised, allowing hundreds of evacuees to return to their homes; the blaze has burned around 7,000 hectares (~25 sq miles). British survivor Malcolm Timbrell, 70, from the village of Bédar, told of surviving in his car while his wife Annette Kilgore and friends died trying to run to safety. A British man died while on the phone to his wife after returning to rescue cats, and two British hikers were found alive but badly burned in a ravine. A 93-year-old British woman admitted Friday with 20% burns to Torrecardenas University Hospital died Sunday night. Separately, a wildfire of 'exceptional scale' is burning near Paris amid France's third heat wave since May, adding to Europe's worsening fire crisis. In the UK, major incidents have been declared in North Wales and in Glossop, Derbyshire in the Peak District, with at least 10 wildfires burning across Wales and 19 separate wildfires being tackled across the UK overall. A wildfire near Conwy Mountain prompted evacuation of 36 homes. A 20-year-old woman, Shania Care-Slede, has been charged with aggravated arson in connection with a UK moor fire for which a major incident was declared. The Met Office's Fire Severity Index identifies parts of southern England — including around Chichester and Bognor Regis in West Sussex — as most at risk. An 'exceptional' wildfire warning has been issued for parts of the UK as a heatwave, now entering its second week in some areas, is forecast to last at least another week; hosepipe bans are in effect. The National Fire Chiefs Council warned that hot dry weather 'significantly increases wildfire risk.' Climatologist Jean-Pascal Van Ypersele warned 'We are not prepared enough for the conditions that fuel these fires.' In a separate legal development, Sánchez's brother David has been banned from holding public office for nine years after being convicted of administrative misconduct relating to his hiring by a socialist-led council in Extremadura.

clusters.state_of_play: The death toll from the major wildfire in southern Spain's Andalusia/Almería region stands at 13, with nationality now confirmed: five Britons, three Belgians, one French national, and one Spanish national among the dead; DNA identification was required for badly burned victims. Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez visited the wildfire site in Almería, met firefighters and emergency crews, and called for Spain to strengthen prevention measures. Victims' families have alleged they received no evacuation order from authorities. The missing count has been revised down to 10 as the fire stabilised, allowing hundreds of evacuees to return to their homes; the blaze has burned around 7,000 hectares (~25 sq miles). British survivor Malcolm Timbrell, 70, from the village of Bédar, told of surviving in his car while his wife Annette Kilgore and friends died trying to run to safety. A British man died while on the phone to his wife after returning to rescue cats, and two British hikers were found alive but badly burned in a ravine. A 93-year-old British woman admitted Friday with 20% burns to Torrecardenas University Hospital died Sunday night. Separately, a wildfire of 'exceptional scale' is burning near Paris amid France's third heat wave since May, adding to Europe's worsening fire crisis. In the UK, major incidents have been declared in North Wales and in Glossop, Derbyshire in the Peak District, with at least 10 wildfires burning across Wales and 19 separate wildfires being tackled across the UK overall. A wildfire near Conwy Mountain prompted evacuation of 36 homes. A 20-year-old woman, Shania Care-Slede, has been charged with aggravated arson in connection with a UK moor fire for which a major incident was declared. The Met Office's Fire Severity Index identifies parts of southern England — including around Chichester and Bognor Regis in West Sussex — as most at risk. An 'exceptional' wildfire warning has been issued for parts of the UK as a heatwave, now entering its second week in some areas, is forecast to last at least another week; hosepipe bans are in effect. The National Fire Chiefs Council warned that hot dry weather 'significantly increases wildfire risk.' Climatologist Jean-Pascal Van Ypersele warned 'We are not prepared enough for the conditions that fuel these fires.' In a separate legal development, Sánchez's brother David has been banned from holding public office for nine years after being convicted of administrative misconduct relating to his hiring by a socialist-led council in Extremadura.

Firefighters are expected to remain on scene for days, if not weeks. Police have arrested two people suspected of deliberately starting the fire; investigators found ten ignition points near the origin. Around 1,000 people have been evacuated. Officials described the blaze as of 'exceptional scale', with road and rail links disrupted. Some 400 firefighters and two waterbombing aircraft have been deployed. The fire coincides with France's third heatwave since May, which forced early closures of the Eiffel Tower, Louvre, and Musée d'Orsay, and led many towns to cancel Bastille Day fireworks displays.

clusters.state_of_play: The UK and EU have signed a post-Brexit Gibraltar treaty at a Brussels ceremony, removing the land border between Gibraltar and Spain and allowing Gibraltar residents to cross using residence cards and Spanish citizens using government ID. Tory and Reform MPs are warning this represents a foreign policy 'betrayal' and that Falklands sovereignty could be Labour's next concession. Andy Burnham has secured 349 Labour MP nominations — including all eligible cabinet members — making it impossible for any rival to challenge him, and is confirmed as Britain's next Prime Minister, expected to take office on 20 July. Burnham has pledged a 'broad church' cabinet and party culture, is considering a larger autumn Budget with allies lobbying for a land tax, public control of utilities and expanded devolution. A new Real Rates Reform Alliance is now also pressing him to go further on business rates reform, calling for a 2% online sales tax to fund a 37% cut in rates for physical retailers. He plans to scrap David Lammy's jury-trial abolition proposals. He voted to back immigration curbs at the Immigration and Asylum Bill's second reading despite a threatened left-wing revolt. Burnham has not uttered a word in the Commons chamber since being sworn in as Makerfield MP on 22 June. Tories are demanding Parliament delay its summer recess to scrutinise him before he takes office. The Reform UK/Farage financial scrutiny story continues: the £5m crypto donor is now linked to Tether, a giant and secretive cryptocurrency firm that Farage has publicly championed. Separately, Farage refused taxpayer-funded security as inadequate, with Reform UK continuing to fund his personal protection.

clusters.state_of_play: The death toll from the major wildfire in southern Spain's Andalusia/Almería region stands at 13, with nationality now confirmed: five Britons, three Belgians, one French national, and one Spanish national among the dead; DNA identification was required for badly burned victims. Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez visited the wildfire site in Almería, met firefighters and emergency crews, and called for Spain to strengthen prevention measures. Victims' families have alleged they received no evacuation order from authorities. The missing count has been revised down to 10 as the fire stabilised, allowing hundreds of evacuees to return to their homes; the blaze has burned around 7,000 hectares (~25 sq miles). British survivor Malcolm Timbrell, 70, from the village of Bédar, told of surviving in his car while his wife Annette Kilgore and friends died trying to run to safety. A British man died while on the phone to his wife after returning to rescue cats, and two British hikers were found alive but badly burned in a ravine. A 93-year-old British woman admitted Friday with 20% burns to Torrecardenas University Hospital died Sunday night. Separately, a wildfire of 'exceptional scale' is burning near Paris amid France's third heat wave since May, adding to Europe's worsening fire crisis. In the UK, major incidents have been declared in North Wales and in Glossop, Derbyshire in the Peak District, with at least 10 wildfires burning across Wales and 19 separate wildfires being tackled across the UK overall. A wildfire near Conwy Mountain prompted evacuation of 36 homes. A 20-year-old woman, Shania Care-Slede, has been charged with aggravated arson in connection with a UK moor fire for which a major incident was declared. The Met Office's Fire Severity Index identifies parts of southern England — including around Chichester and Bognor Regis in West Sussex — as most at risk. An 'exceptional' wildfire warning has been issued for parts of the UK as a heatwave, now entering its second week in some areas, is forecast to last at least another week; hosepipe bans are in effect. The National Fire Chiefs Council warned that hot dry weather 'significantly increases wildfire risk.' Climatologist Jean-Pascal Van Ypersele warned 'We are not prepared enough for the conditions that fuel these fires.' In a separate legal development, Sánchez's brother David has been banned from holding public office for nine years after being convicted of administrative misconduct relating to his hiring by a socialist-led council in Extremadura.

items.title: UK hit by widespread ‘firewave’ as wildfire risk grows, experts warn

ledger.what_new: 19 separate wildfires being tackled across the UK, per officials.
ledger.unique: Specific updated count of 19 active UK wildfires from official source.

clusters.state_of_play: The death toll from the major wildfire in southern Spain's Andalusia/Almería region stands at 13, with nationality now confirmed: five Britons, three Belgians, one French national, and one Spanish national among the dead; DNA identification was required for badly burned victims. Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez visited the wildfire site in Almería, met firefighters and emergency crews, and called for Spain to strengthen prevention measures. Victims' families have alleged they received no evacuation order from authorities. The missing count has been revised down to 10 as the fire stabilised, allowing hundreds of evacuees to return to their homes; the blaze has burned around 7,000 hectares (~25 sq miles). British survivor Malcolm Timbrell, 70, from the village of Bédar, told of surviving in his car while his wife Annette Kilgore and friends died trying to run to safety. A British man died while on the phone to his wife after returning to rescue cats, and two British hikers were found alive but badly burned in a ravine. A 93-year-old British woman admitted Friday with 20% burns to Torrecardenas University Hospital died Sunday night. Separately, a wildfire of 'exceptional scale' is burning near Paris amid France's third heat wave since May, adding to Europe's worsening fire crisis. In the UK, major incidents have been declared in North Wales and in Glossop, Derbyshire in the Peak District, with at least 10 wildfires burning across Wales and 19 separate wildfires being tackled across the UK overall. A wildfire near Conwy Mountain prompted evacuation of 36 homes. A 20-year-old woman, Shania Care-Slede, has been charged with aggravated arson in connection with a UK moor fire for which a major incident was declared. The Met Office's Fire Severity Index identifies parts of southern England — including around Chichester and Bognor Regis in West Sussex — as most at risk. An 'exceptional' wildfire warning has been issued for parts of the UK as a heatwave, now entering its second week in some areas, is forecast to last at least another week; hosepipe bans are in effect. The National Fire Chiefs Council warned that hot dry weather 'significantly increases wildfire risk.' Climatologist Jean-Pascal Van Ypersele warned 'We are not prepared enough for the conditions that fuel these fires.' In a separate legal development, Sánchez's brother David has been banned from holding public office for nine years after being convicted of administrative misconduct relating to his hiring by a socialist-led council in Extremadura.

June CPI came in weaker than expected, lifting S&P 500 futures. SpaceX stock is falling for a second straight day, nearing its $135 IPO price, one month after its record debut and a week after being added to the Nasdaq-100. Analysts flag 'tectonic' risks despite the bumper results.
